# `protocol_single_participant`: a protocol names only one role

A protocol describes a conversation between roles, so it needs at least
two. This warning means every step names the same role. The only way to write
that is a role sending to itself, which is also an error (`protocol_invalid`),
so the two are reported together.

## A program that triggers it

```march
mod Main do
  type A = A
  protocol Solo do
    A -> A : Int
  end
  fn main() do () end
end
```

`Solo` has `A` sending to `A`. There is no one else to talk to.

## The fix

Name the role on the other end of each message:

```march
mod Main do
  type A = A
  type B = B
  protocol Duo do
    A -> B : Int
  end
  fn main() do () end
end
```

## Why the rule exists

A message with the same sender and receiver goes nowhere: there is no
peer to wait for it or reply to it. A protocol with one role cannot be split
into two endpoints for `Chan.new`, or into role modules.

See also: [declaring a protocol](../session-types.md#declaring-a-protocol).
